domain: Business and human rights / non-judicial grievance mechanisms: OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises specific instances (RBC / corporate accountability)
prediction_question: At the filing instant of a specific instance - the day an interested party (individual, NGO, trade union, business or other submitter) submits a complaint to a National Contact Point (NCP) alleging that a multinational enterprise did not observe the OECD Guidelines - will the NCP accept the case for further examination at initial assessment (Step 3 of the procedure), or will the case be closed without proceeding ('not accepted', which per the publisher's own terminology also includes withdrawals before the initial assessment completes)? A useful prediction tells complainants whether and how a grievance framed this way is likely to clear the intake gate of the chosen NCP, tells companies and RBC observers which complaint profiles are likely to enter mediation, and gives the 52-NCP network a measurable intake-consistency signal across the functional-equivalence agenda the OECD itself tracks. Acceptance is a real institutional decision published 1-12+ months after filing (measured: 2021-2025 closed-cohort acceptance 54-63%), not an editorial artefact.
prediction_time: One sentence: the prediction is made on the submission date of the specific instance (day grain; the NCP-recorded 'Date' field on the case record), using only the complaint's own DB-coded attributes (lead NCP, supporting NCP, country of the issue, submitter class, sector/subsector, Guidelines topics and subtopics cited, entity-involved type) plus trailing history computed only from cases whose initial assessment was already decided before that date, and the label is the initial-assessment decision that the NCP publishes strictly afterwards. Dated example (Europe/Paris, publisher HQ; all dates recorded by the publisher at day grain, no time of day): case kr0029, Hoang Gia Trading & Services vs Lotte Corporation; feature event window = all specific instances with submission date < 2026-02-27 and decision-published before the instant (trailing acceptance rates, counts per NCP/submitter/topic); first-available timestamps and version = the complaint itself exists 2026-02-27 (Korean NCP, filed 2026-02-27 local; the DB's own listing date for this case equals the filing date - measured, see measurements.db_listing_lag), and the case's structured attributes are as coded in the current database vintage (fetched 2026-11-03; the database migrated platform in June 2025 and no historical vintages are archived - current-vintage posture, explicit assumption); eligibility cutoff = submission date in a scored window AND terminal status at the extraction vintage ('In progress' cases are excluded, not labelled); prediction instant = 2026-02-27 00:00 Europe/Paris (day-grain convention stated); target start/end = the initial assessment event, published 2026-05-21 (Korean NCP statement, decision 'not accepted'), i.e. target window 2026-02-27..2026-05-21 ending at the decision - every part of the target window is after the instant; the DB listing date (2026-02-27 for this case) is never used as instant or decision date. For any future-event scoring, a row scored at filing must use only rows decided strictly before its filing date for history features.
target_definition: Binary label per specific instance: 1 = the NCP accepted the case for further examination at initial assessment (DB Status values indicating acceptance: 'Concluded' after acceptance, or an in-progress-but-accepted state; the publisher's status taxonomy from the case records and the annual reports: closed = concluded OR not accepted, in progress = awaiting initial assessment OR accepted and ongoing); 0 = the case did not proceed past initial assessment ('Not accepted', which the publisher defines to include cases withdrawn prior to completion of the initial assessment). Source columns: the DB case-record 'Status' field (label source; excludable - not shipped as a feature) with 'Outcomes', 'Procedural issues' and all prose summaries excluded from features as post-hoc. Rows with Status 'In progress' at extraction are excluded from scored splits (censored, not negative). Label derivation needs no external data and no threshold.

split_strategy: PROPOSED windows by submission year, disjoint; exact per-window row and label counts are the FIRST construction measurement (they require the full 700-case scrape - bulk work, worker), so the numbers below are the publisher's own reported aggregates plus measured closed-cohort acceptance rates, never presented as full-DB counts. Unit = one specific instance (DB case ID). Train: filings 2000-2017 (publisher filings table 2011-2017 sums to 217; pre-2011 filings approximately 203 from DB total 700 minus 2011-2025 - approximate, to be measured exactly at construction). Eval: filings 2018-2021 (189 per the publisher's table; all resolved by extraction - measured 2021 cohort: 63% accepted/37% not accepted). Holdout: filings 2022-2024 (152 per the publisher's table, minus rows still 'In progress' at extraction; measured cohort acceptance 2024: 58%, 2025: 54%). 2025-2026 filings are EXCLUDED from scored rows: the 2025 cohort is mostly still pending (publisher's data annex: at end-2025, of the 120 received in 2025, 99 in progress, 19 not accepted, 2 concluded; restricted-marked annex cited as cross-check only - construction re-measures censoring exactly from the DB). Both classes measured in every recent closed cohort (2021: 27/16, 2024: 30/22, 2025: 30/26). Cluster structure to measure at construction: cases cluster by lead NCP (top-5 NCPs hold 52% of 2025 submissions), by respondent company (repeat filings against the same company occur, incl. coordinated multi-NCP campaigns), and by submission year (the 2025 individual-submission surge is a cohort effect: 71% of 2025 submissions vs 23% in 2024) - the clustered count and an interval on it are required outputs of the first construction measurement, per the discovery policy.

review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (2026-11-03, discovery-only session; no construction, no worker). (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - class A: OECD T&C grant Data use 'for any purpose, even for commercial use' absent additional restrictions, none found on the database or case pages; 2025 annual report is explicitly CC BY 4.0; attribution format prescribed ('[OECD (year), Title, URL]') and carried into LICENSE.md; the restricted-marked annual-report data annexes are excluded from any redistributed artifact. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED with one recorded assumption - instant = submission date (day grain, publisher-recorded per case), label event strictly after (initial assessment published 1-12+ months later; measured kr0029: filed 2026-02-27, decided 2026-05-21); the DB-coded complaint attributes (NCP, issue country, submitter class, sector, topics cited) are complaint-stated, but the codification itself is NCP/OECD-assigned in the current vintage - an ASSUMPTION to verify at construction on a bounded sample (compare DB topic codes against the complaint text in the linked initial-assessment statements; a material mismatch downgrades those columns to post-hoc and they are dropped); DB listing dates measured as unusable for timing (0 to ~32-month lag); current-vintage posture explicit (DB migrated platform June 2025, no historical vintages; inclusion timing discretionary per the publisher's FAQ - quoted). (3) Target SUPPORTED - binary acceptance at initial assessment derived from the publisher's own Status taxonomy (quoted Box-terminology: closed = concluded OR not accepted, incl. pre-assessment withdrawals; in progress = pending); label source column excludable (Status/Outcomes/Procedural issues/summaries never shipped as features); censoring handled by eligibility (terminal status at extraction), not by treating pending as negative. (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED at the aggregate level - publisher-measured filings/year for every proposed window (train ~420, eval 189, holdout 152 minus pending), both classes measured in the 2021/2024/2025 closed cohorts (63%/58%/54% accepted) and strongly varying by submitter class (39-86% in 2025); exact per-window counts, the pending fraction of 2022-2024 filings and the clustered counts (by NCP, by respondent company, by year) are the first construction measurement on the worker - this record never presents those as known. (5) Not a mirror SUPPORTED as differentiated - the OECD publishes the registry and aggregate reports but no prediction task; the nearest prior art is an academic hand-coded dataset of 81 human-rights cases concluded 2012-2021 scored on remedy gravity (Springer chapter, descriptive, not distributed in ML-ready form, different population and different target), named in the novelty check; no ML-ready NCP acceptance/conclusion benchmark found in catalog or literature searches. RISKS named for the construction gate: (a) the WB-instrument-family defect - if a trailing NCP(+submitter-class) rate table matches the model, there is no headroom and the candidate drops at baseline (the reference triad is therefore mandatory: global prior, NCP trailing rate, NCP x submitter-class trailing rate); (b) topic-codification timing (assumption above); (c) small-population clustering (top-5 NCPs = 52% of recent filings; ~120-190 rows per window) - the honest effective-sample and cluster counts must accompany any quoted score.
next_action: Hand to construction (worker; discovery is complete and no construction was run in this session): (1) scrape the 700 case records via the RSS enumeration (47 pages) + JS-rendered case pages, freeze the extraction with sha256 and the DB vintage timestamp, and measure exactly: per-window row counts, label counts, pending fraction of 2022-2024 filings, clustered counts by lead NCP / respondent company / submission year; (2) verify the topic-codification assumption on a bounded sample (DB topics vs complaint text in the linked initial-assessment statements) and drop any column that fails; (3) build the trailing-history features with the strictly-before rule (only cases decided before the instant contribute to history), enforce the restricted prediction protocol for the self-answer join (a scored row's label is a later row's history operand - same coupling class as za-statsa: ship pre-computed fixed-window feature matrices or strip case keys so no solver-visible join couples two scored rows), run gate-1.5 reverse-history probes on the exact artifact; (4) triad references mandatory: global prior, trailing NCP rate table, trailing NCP x submitter-class rate table - if the model does not beat them, record no-headroom and stop (WB-instrument-family defect); (5) splits: train 2000-2017 / eval 2018-2021 / holdout 2022-2024 by submission year, 2025+ excluded as censored (re-check at extraction); (6) LICENSE.md: '[OECD (2026), Database of specific instances handled by National Contact Points, <URL>]' attribution, CC BY 4.0 carry-through for any annual-report-derived text (none planned), the restricted-annex exclusion note, the current-vintage/retrospective as-of statement in the dataset card; (7) full-worker qualification -> exact-byte acceptance before any AUC or headroom number is quoted.

novelty_check.ours: Full-population, all-topics intake-acceptance prediction task at the filing instant of an OECD Guidelines specific instance (complainant class, sector, Guidelines chapters cited, issue country, lead NCP + strictly-prior trailing history -> accepted for further examination at initial assessment y/n), built from the OECD's own case-level registry (700 cases since 2000) with terminal-status eligibility, submission-year temporal splits (train 2000-2017 / eval 2018-2021 / holdout 2022-2024) and a scored contract; no such task exists in ML-ready form
